description.p: StillStream is a ten-foot Twitch client for Linux living rooms and handhelds. It is built for a gamepad or a TV remote: every screen is reachable with a D-pad, four arrows and two buttons, so nothing needs a mouse or a keyboard.

Live streams and past broadcasts play in Twitch's own player, so channels, quality options and captions behave the way they do on the web, inside a full-screen interface that scales from a handheld display to a 4K television.

ul.li: Browse Home, Following and categories, page through results and search for channels
Resume past broadcasts where you left them from a Continue Watching shelf
Keep favourite channels on the home screen
Follow live chat next to the player and reply with an on-screen keyboard
Choose playback quality and toggle closed captions from the player
Sign in once with Twitch, or with a device code and a scannable QR code, or watch as a guest

description.p: Personalised screens such as Following need a Twitch account; guest browsing, search and playback work without signing in. StillStream is an independent project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Twitch Interactive, Inc.

ul.li: Releases are published to a signed Flatpak repository with a stable and a beta (pre-release) branch, so installs update through Discover or flatpak update.
Settings has an Updates card: it says when a new version is out, how to get it for Flatpak or AppImage, and whether to include pre-releases. A dot on Settings marks a new version.

description.p: Live previews in the player, for testing.

ul.li: The Following panel in the player (Down) previews the selected channel too.
With "Play live previews with sound" on, the stream being watched is muted while a preview plays and comes back when you move on; otherwise previews stay silent.
"Updating…" now replaces the channel count above the divider instead of pushing the streams down on every refresh.
No fixed one-second wait: the preview loads 0.4 seconds after a card is selected and appears as soon as its video plays.
The preview only covers the thumbnail once its video is playing, so Twitch's paused poster no longer flashes.
New Player behaviour setting: play live previews with sound.
The preview starts muted while still hidden behind the thumbnail, so it is already running when it shows.
Twitch's paused poster is started even before the player has created its video.
A player that still refuses to start is described in the terminal output.
When Twitch leaves a player on its paused poster, the app presses Twitch's own play button and starts Twitch's media player directly.
The preview player runs at the minimum size Twitch requires for autoplay and is scaled down onto the card, so it plays instead of showing its poster.
It starts loading hidden behind the thumbnail right away, so the video is ready when it shows after one second.
The Flatpak gets the same device access as other controller-first Electron apps, so Chromium can read every kind of controller.

description.p: Controller and preview fixes, for testing.

ul.li: The Flatpak can read the udev device database, which Chromium needs to see Xbox controllers and Steam Input's virtual controller.
Live previews actually play, and start after one second.
A live channel's card plays a muted preview after it has been selected for 1.5 seconds.
The sidebar logo sits a little lower, closer to its wordmark.
Xbox and other XInput-style controllers now work on SteamOS, with or without Steam Input: every connected controller is read, not only the first one listed.
Controllers without a recognised layout have their buttons and d-pad translated.
Settings lists the controllers the app can see and the buttons each one reports.

description.p: VacuumStream is now StillStream, with a new icon.

ul.li: The first release under the new name, built from the 0.2.1-fork.13 test builds: fullscreen-first player with an overlay control bar, a Following panel, chat over the video, one-step Twitch sign-in for ad-free subscriptions, low latency, remembered quality and TV remote support.
The application ID is now io.github.karasune.StillStream, so it installs as a new app. Preferences, favourites and watch progress carry over where the old data is reachable; sign in once again.
The fullscreen control bar closes with Down as well as Up and Back, like the Following panel.
Up and Down in the sidebar move between tabs only, so Down from Search reaches Settings instead of the on-screen keyboard.
Left from Settings returns to the tab you came from instead of the Settings tab.
New option to pause a stream while another app has focus and resume it on return.
Start screen, fullscreen and pause options are grouped in a Player behaviour card.
Down closes the Following panel as well as opening it, the same way Up opens and closes the control bar.
With a mouse in fullscreen, the top edge shows the control bar and the bottom edge the Following panel; each hides 1.5 seconds after the pointer leaves it.
The fullscreen control bar takes focus again, on opening a stream and when shown with Up, so it can be navigated with a controller or remote.
The bar hides after five seconds without input, and stays up while one of its menus is open.
The Start screen options in Settings keep their normal size.
Streams open in fullscreen, with the control bar shown on top for a few seconds.
Up shows or hides the control bar; Back hides it before leaving fullscreen.
A Settings switch keeps the windowed player for desktop use.
No grey haze over the stream when the mouse rests on it in stream fullscreen.
The live panel button is now "Following", beside Back, away from the playback controls.

description.p: TV controls, live panel and chat overlay.

ul.li: In stream fullscreen, OK, Space and A play or pause instead of leaving; Back leaves.
A live panel along the bottom lists followed channels that are live; open it with Down in fullscreen or the Following button, and switch streams without leaving fullscreen.
Chat can be shown over the video, also in fullscreen, with position, size, opacity and text size settings. Chat is dark by default.
A low latency switch for live streams in the Quality menu.
The chosen quality is remembered for new streams.
The start screen option now toggles with a TV remote's OK button, not only with a controller or Space.
Streams start at full volume instead of Twitch's half-volume default, so they match the rest of the system.
A Settings option opens Following instead of Home at startup, after leaving a stream and on Back.
Twitch's sign-in pages inside the app scale with the screen: 100% at 1080p, 200% at 1440p and 250% at 4K.
Ctrl and plus, minus or 0 fine-tune or reset that zoom.
In Steam Game Mode, or whenever the app is fullscreen, Twitch sign-in opens inside the app window instead of a separate window that gamescope stretched across the screen.
Escape, or B on a controller, closes the sign-in page without also leaving Settings.
Clicking the video in stream fullscreen no longer traps the keyboard; a click now brings the controls back.
Escape always returns control to the app after the video was clicked.

description.p: First release of the Karasune fork.

ul.li: The player fullscreen button now fills the screen with the stream and hides the controls; Back or Enter brings them back.
The screen no longer dims or locks while a stream is playing.
One Sign in with Twitch action signs in both the app and the player, so subscriber and Turbo ad-free benefits apply.
Application metadata is ready for store listings: screenshots, brand colours and content rating.
An npm lockfile is shipped so the app can be built offline from source.

description.p: The first release where a controller is genuinely enough.

ul.li: Seek and resume past broadcasts, pick quality and toggle captions from the player.
Browse categories, page through Home and Following, and save favourite channels.
Live chat beside the player, reachable without a mouse.
Controller-first sign-in with a device code and a QR code.
The interface was rebuilt on Twitch's own colour and type tokens.

description.p: Better controller text entry and more reliable playback start.

ul.li: An always-available on-screen keyboard in Search.
Live streams retry startup and unmute once playback really progresses.
Manual play and mute controls cancel automatic retries.

description.p: Playback, sign-in and account persistence fixes.

ul.li: Streams start muted with controller-accessible play and pause controls.
Sign-in shows a scannable QR code alongside the activation link.
Tokens prefer the system keyring, with an owner-only file as fallback.
Gamepad, arrow-key and remote navigation across every screen.
Guest quick watch, channel search and Twitch account sign-in.
Twitch live and past-broadcast playback from handheld displays up to 4K.
